title: Global Oil Markets — Executive Daily Brief (Saturday, 22 August 2026)
executive_summary: Four developments with highest market consequence today: (1) Panama Canal postpones a planned Aug-26 draft cut and adjusts August transit measures, shaping USGC–Asia refined-product/LPG routing and demurrage through early September. (2) Iraq–Turkey one‑year deal keeps Ceyhan crude exports flowing; first tanker already loaded under the new framework, stabilizing Med sour supply. (3) ARA product balances diverge in August-to‑date: fuel oil builds while gasoil/diesel trend lower, firming NWE middle‑distillate cracks. (4) US weekly data show a distillate draw into mid‑August while crude/gasoline rose, supporting diesel spreads on the USGC and Atlantic Basin arbitrage economics.

developments.headline: Panama Canal tweaks: draft cut postponed to Sep-2; transit/auction adjustments remain amid low Gatun Lake levels
developments.summary: The Panama Canal Authority (ACP) signaled near‑term relief by postponing the Neopanamax draft reduction (48.0 ft TFW) that had been slated for Aug-26 to Sep-2, 2026. ACP also confirmed temporary changes to transit auctions and daily slot management due to reduced precipitation. Net effect: product and LPG cargoes ex‑USGC to Pacific Basin retain slightly better loading flexibility through end‑August, but voyage times and queue risk remain elevated into September.
developments.why_it_matters: Even modest draft/daily-slot shifts alter liftability, parcel sizing, and freight for USGC → West Coast LatAm/Asia gasoline, diesel, jet, and LPG flows. Any renewed tightening from early September could widen trans‑Pacific clean and LPG route premia and re‑activate rerouting via Cape of Good Hope for time‑sensitive cargoes.

developments.headline: Ceyhan exports sustained: Iraq–Turkey one‑year pipeline/exports accord in force; first cargo loaded
developments.summary: Baghdad and Ankara implemented a one‑year crude transportation/exexport agreement on Aug-1, maintaining Iraq‑to‑Ceyhan flows via the Iraq–Turkey Pipeline after the prior treaty lapsed Jul-27. Iraq Oil Report and MEES confirm the first tanker loading at Ceyhan under the new terms earlier in August.
developments.why_it_matters: Sustained northern Iraqi flows steady Med sour availability (Kirkuk/SOMO streams) and help backfill Hormuz‑risk‑sensitive European refiners. Supports prompt Med differentials vs Dated and eases pressure on Urals/medium‑sour replacements. Watch for volume cadence vs prior months and any Kurdish offtake dynamics.

developments.headline: ARA hub: August fuel oil builds; gasoil/diesel trend lower
developments.summary: Insights Global data reported by Engine show ARA independent fuel oil stocks averaging about 9–10% higher MTD vs July, while gasoil (diesel/heating oil) inventories are lower MTD. Separate mid‑June reporting showed gasoil/jet inventories below seasonal norms, a pattern consistent with tighter middle‑distillate balances into late summer.
developments.why_it_matters: Lower ARA gasoil amplifies support for NWE diesel cracks and front‑month spreads, with spillovers to ARA/Rotterdam premiums and barge pricing. Fuel oil builds can cap HSFO cracks and influence bunkering economics in NWE.

developments.headline: US weekly stats: mid‑Aug distillate draw; crude and gasoline up on week
developments.summary: EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report (week ending Aug-14; released Aug-19) shows distillate stocks fell w/w, while crude and gasoline inventories increased. PADD 3 utilization and product supplied patterns indicate steady diesel demand and shoulder‑season gasoline balancing.
developments.why_it_matters: A distillate draw supports USGC ULSD cracks and export arbs to LatAm/Europe. Rising crude/gasoline stocks can soften RBOB cracks unless export pull tightens. Physical buyers on the USGC should expect firmer diesel basis vs gasoline into late August.

developments.headline: USGC refining: incident reported at Marathon Galveston Bay coker this week
developments.summary: Reuters incident reports indicate a coking unit issue at Marathon’s Galveston Bay refinery (Texas City) on Aug-20, following an earlier minor leak notice on Aug-10. No formal multi‑day outage guidance was issued in public reports as of today.
developments.why_it_matters: Any coker constraint can tighten USGC gasoline/jet components and reduce HGO/LSGO output at the margin, modestly supporting product cracks and regional basis if duration extends. Monitor for unit rate impacts into next week.

portfolio_implications: Maintain constructive bias on NWE and USGC diesel cracks into late August given ARA gasoil draw tendencies and EIA‑reported US distillate draw.
For trans‑Pacific clean/LPG exposure, keep optionality on Panama vs Cape routings through early September; watch ACP advisories for draft/slot changes that could widen clean LR freight spreads.
Keep selective length in Med sour grades (Kirkuk/SOMO) and Med cracks; Ceyhan continuity reduces extreme tightness risk but monitor flow cadence.
USGC physical buyers: consider advancing ULSD procurement; gasoline exposures remain more balanced given inventory builds.
Refining equities with coking exposure on the USGC could see short‑term margin support if unit constraints persist; treat as tactical, not structural.
risks: Weather: Atlantic tropics remain active seasonally, but as of Aug-21 NHC outlook shows no immediate Gulf threats; a surprise USGC storm would quickly alter runs and product balances.
Policy/sanctions: Any escalation affecting Iraq–Turkey pipeline terms or Med terminal security would re‑price Med sours and freight.
Canal hydrology: Faster‑than‑expected Gatun Lake declines could re‑tighten Panama drafts/slots in early September, raising demurrage and re‑routing costs.
Chokepoints: Red Sea/Bab el‑Mandeb tanker flows remain inconsistent; a deterioration would divert more clean/dirty tonnage via the Cape, lifting global freight and delivered product prices.
opportunities: Exploit diesel strength vs gasoline via crack/basis structures in NWE and USGC.
Time‑charter or optional voyage positions on LR/MR clean tonnage with Cape/Panama flexibility for September loadings.
Target Med sour crude diffs and refinery margin hedges benefiting from steadier Ceyhan flows.
watch_items: ACP Advisories to Shipping through Sep‑2 and any draft/slot revisions; reassess routing economics daily.
EIA Aug-21–28 data next Wednesday (Aug‑26) for confirmation of US distillate trend.
FOIZ weekly stock print due mid‑week for confirmation of Fujairah light/middle trends.
Any formal statements from Iraq’s SOMO/KRG on Ceyhan volume cadence and quality slates.
USGC refinery notices (Marathon Galveston Bay and peers) for unit status updates.
